---
title: "T-5 adjudication — the covr shard-4 death: an installed-copy masquerade defeated two source-scan locators (one loud, one silent)"
---

Date: 2026-11-28. Task: review-06 §9 T-5 / §5a. Evidence: scheduled run
46012520485 (coverage job failure, shard-4 `covr-failed`), plus a local
reproduction on macOS with covr 3.6.5 + S7 0.2.2 that failed
byte-for-signature (the fragments `_bundled())` and `Not yet available:`
match the CI transcript tail exactly), so the defect is deterministic,
not platform- or float-class. The full `msuiter-tests/testthat.Rout.fail`
was recovered from the repro through a capture-patched
`covr:::show_failures` (covr 3.6.5 keeps only the slice from the first
`^>` line of the fail file in its error condition and deletes the
install tree on exit — the reason CI could never see the failing
expectation from the tail-25 transcript group).

## 1. The failing expectation (read from the recovered Rout.fail)

```
FILE[coverage#4] test-abort-contract.R
FAIL[coverage#4] every msuiter_abort() call carries the mandatory i/j/c payload
  : `total` is not strictly more than 100L. Difference: -100
```

The very first roster file; the whole shard then attests vacuous
(`covr-failed`), the census reddens, and the chained test-heavy job
cancels — the nine-red-nights shape after #141 removed the covr float
class and exposed this REAL test failure underneath.

## 2. Root cause (one sentence, then the mechanism)

`test-abort-contract.R`'s `.abort_root()` walks upward from
`testthat::test_path()` looking for a DESCRIPTION that declares
`Package: msuiter` — under covr the tests run as `<pkg>-tests` BESIDE
the installed copy (`testInstalledPackage`), so the walk's very first
parent IS the installed package: its DESCRIPTION passes the name test,
the census then scans `list.files(<installed>/R)` — which holds no
`*.R` sources — reads zero call sites, and the file's own
window-liveness guard (`expect_gt(total, 100L)`) fires exactly as
designed. In the normal check layout the walk finds no DESCRIPTION
ancestry and the sanctioned skip speaks; in the repo layout the real
checkout is found and the scan runs at full strength (386 call sites on
today's tree). The installed-copy masquerade is the only third context,
and this locator did not know it.

**The silent twin.** `test-rng-hygiene.R`'s `.rh_root()` carries the
same hole — but with no liveness guard, so under covr it scanned an
empty roster and PASSED BLIND (`offenders == character()` on zero
files): a vacuous green of exactly the class the census law of
2026-10-24 was written to make impossible. Fixed in the same commit;
this is why the fix touches two files and not one.

## 3. The fix (the banked discriminator, not a new law)

`helper-check-layout.R` already solved this context class for the
scenario laws (the `.ms_root` Built: discriminator — an installed
DESCRIPTION carries INSTALL's `Built:` stamp, a checkout does not;
banked at run 39536641469, "covr coverage failed under instrumentation").
Both locators now require `any(^Package: msuiter)` AND
`!any(^Built:)`. Context behavior after the fix:

- **repo mode** (devtools/testthat at the checkout): unchanged — the
  source root is found, both scans run in full.
- **check layout** (simulated sibling copies): unchanged — no
  DESCRIPTION ancestry, sanctioned skip.
- **covr installed copy**: the walk now refuses the installed
  DESCRIPTION (Built: stamp) and correctly finds NO source root — both
  source-scan units skip honestly (the same intra-file skip class the
  attested scenario-law skips already form), the firing-control units
  still execute, shard 4 attests `status=ok` with the roster fully
  visited, and the empty active ledger stays lawful (the census law's
  "a row that sanctions nothing is itself a defect" is why no
  `covr-divergences.tsv` row is added: there is no shard-level
  divergence to sanction).

## 4. The diagnosability repair (review-06 5a-i, independent of the fix)

`scheduled.yml`'s coverage job gains two failure-only steps after the
existing echo step: snapshot any `covr-lib*` fail transcripts into
`covr-logs/`, then upload `covr-logs/` as an artifact. Green nights
never pay artifact rent; the next CI death names its own expectation.

## 5. Verification

- Local targeted covr mini-shard (real `tools/ci/run-covr-shard.R`,
  mini manifest of the two fixed files): attests `status=ok`, no
  `covr-failed`, skips present for the two source-scan units.
- Repo-mode run of both files at the checkout: green (the scans execute
  against the real tree).
- CI: the coverage leg re-dispatched on the repaired ref must census
  `shards=4/4` with shard 4 ok — the adjudication gate for this task.
